verses.1: The three men ceased to answer Job, for they saw that he was righteous in his own eyes.
verses.2: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, from the family of Ram, became greatly angry with Job. His anger burned against Job because Job justified himself before God.
verses.3: His anger burned also against the three friends, because they had failed to find an answer, and had instead declared Job guilty.
verses.4: Elihu waited to speak to Job, for they were older than him in years.
verses.5: Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouths of the three men, and his anger burned.
verses.6: Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young in years, but you are the aged. Therefore I held my peace, and feared to declare my knowledge to you.
verses.7: I thought, Days will speak, and many years will make known wisdom.
verses.8: But in truth, it is the spirit in a person, and the breath of the Almighty who gives understanding.
verses.9: The many are not wise, and the aged do not understand justice.
verses.10: Therefore I say, Listen to me, and I will declare my knowledge to you as well.
verses.11: I have listened to your words, and have given ear to your reasonings, until you have made your sayings plain.
verses.12: But I was considering, and behold, there was no one to answer Job, none among you to confute his words.
verses.13: Lest you say, We have found wisdom, and God will not give an answer, though it is a human being.
verses.14: For no arguments were arranged for me, and in your words I did not answer him.
verses.15: I held my peace, for they did not answer. I waited, but they spoke no more.
verses.16: And I waited, for they did not speak. They stood in silence, and answered no more.
verses.17: Therefore I will answer, I too. I too will declare my knowledge.
verses.18: For my words are ready within me, my heart is overfull as if it were wine, restrained no longer.
verses.19: My heart is like new wineskins ready to burst.
verses.20: I will speak, and find relief for myself. I will open my mouth and answer.
verses.21: I will not show partiality to any man, nor will I flatter any person.
verses.22: For I do not know how to flatter, and my Maker will not lift me up.

notes:
Notes
- v. 2: "the family of Ram" — the Hebrew phrase מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת רָם is translated as "from the family of Ram" to preserve the familial connection.
- v. 21: "my Maker will not lift me up" — the Hebrew literally reads "my Maker will not give me weight." The phrase כִּמְעַט יִשָּׂאֵנִי עֹשֵׂנִי is metaphorical, suggesting that if I were to flatter, my Maker would not grant me significance.
raw:
[1] The three men ceased to answer Job, for they saw that he was righteous in his own eyes.

[2] Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, from the family of Ram, became greatly angry with Job. His anger burned against Job because Job justified himself before God.

[3] His anger burned also against the three friends, because they had failed to find an answer, and had instead declared Job guilty.

[4] Elihu waited to speak to Job, for they were older than him in years.

[5] Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouths of the three men, and his anger burned.

[6] Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young in years, but you are the aged. Therefore I held my peace, and feared to declare my knowledge to you.

[7] I thought, Days will speak, and many years will make known wisdom.

[8] But in truth, it is the spirit in a person, and the breath of the Almighty who gives understanding.

[9] The many are not wise, and the aged do not understand justice.

[10] Therefore I say, Listen to me, and I will declare my knowledge to you as well.

[11] I have listened to your words, and have given ear to your reasonings, until you have made your sayings plain.

[12] But I was considering, and behold, there was no one to answer Job, none among you to confute his words.

[13] Lest you say, We have found wisdom, and God will not give an answer, though it is a human being.

[14] For no arguments were arranged for me, and in your words I did not answer him.

[15] I held my peace, for they did not answer. I waited, but they spoke no more.

[16] And I waited, for they did not speak. They stood in silence, and answered no more.

[17] Therefore I will answer, I too. I too will declare my knowledge.

[18] For my words are ready within me, my heart is overfull as if it were wine, restrained no longer.

[19] My heart is like new wineskins ready to burst.

[20] I will speak, and find relief for myself. I will open my mouth and answer.

[21] I will not show partiality to any man, nor will I flatter any person.

[22] For I do not know how to flatter, and my Maker will not lift me up.

---
Notes
- v. 2: "the family of Ram" — the Hebrew phrase מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת רָם is translated as "from the family of Ram" to preserve the familial connection.
- v. 21: "my Maker will not lift me up" — the Hebrew literally reads "my Maker will not give me weight." The phrase כִּמְעַט יִשָּׂאֵנִי עֹשֵׂנִי is metaphorical, suggesting that if I were to flatter, my Maker would not grant me significance.
